content.text:
Build and runtime both check out — server starts cleanly, both routes render with no errors. View transitions are fully wired up. Here's what I did:

**Enabled the feature** — `next.config.ts` now sets `experimental.viewTransition: true`, and `types/react-canary.d.ts` references `react/canary` so TypeScript knows about the `ViewTransition` component that Next's vendored React canary exports.

**Shared element morph** (`app/ProductGrid.tsx:14`, `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:48`) — each grid thumbnail and the detail hero are wrapped in `<ViewTransition name="product-image-<slug>">`. On navigation React pairs the matching names, so the browser morphs the thumbnail into the hero (and back), animating position, size, and aspect ratio. The shared `share="product-image-morph"` class lets the CSS tune the morph's duration and easing.

**Directional page slides** — each page declares its own enter/exit classes: home exits/enters on the left, detail on the right. So going grid → detail, the old page slides out left while the new one slides in from the right (a leftward "forward" sweep), and going back reverses it. Because direction is derived from which page is which rather than from click handlers, browser back/forward buttons get correct directionality for free. The morphing image is lifted out of the slide automatically since it has its own named transition group.

**Suspense transitions** — both boundaries (the grid on home, the product details panel) wrap the fallback in `<ViewTransition exit="suspense-fade-out">` and the content in `<ViewTransition enter="suspense-fade-in">`, so the skeleton fades out while real content fades in with a slight upward drift instead of popping.

**Reduced motion** — a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block in `app/globals.css` sets `animation: none` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements (navigation becomes an instant swap) and also disables the skeleton pulse animation.

One structural note: the detail page previously returned a bare `<div>` while home used `<main>`, so detail content was unpadded and full-width. I wrapped it in `<main>` so both pages share the same centered container — this also keeps the slide and morph geometry consistent between routes.

To see it live: `npm run dev`, click a product card, and watch the colored image morph into the hero while the page slides; the details text fades in from the skeleton ~100ms later. In browsers without the View Transitions API (e.g. older Firefox), everything degrades gracefully to instant navigation.
